new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide: Laycock judges stress non-phonemic in all the Lumi Subdistrict languages he lists and leaves it unmarked when it falls on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa (implying that as the default); he marks it otherwise. For Eitiep specifically nothing is stated: its dozen forms were supplied second-hand, and the published/re-keyed forms carry marks on non-initial syllables in some words (nimáp 'breast', iyén 'sun') and initial in others, so no placement rule for Eitiep can be read from this source.

new_statements.exceptions: none in the windows seen; 'Excrescent vowels between full consonants are reduced in stress' (separate remark on transitional vowels)
new_statements.identity_note: The article covers Eitiep [eit] (entry printed p.43: 380 speakers, villages Wambi, Yadagaro, Yamegil, E. Palei CD = Laycock 1973 no. 46), but Laycock had no Eitiep informant: the Eitiep forms are column 29 of 'Table 2: Supplementary wordlist', a brief list supplied to him by others at Lumi 'in four languages for which I could not myself locate informants'. The stress sentence is a survey-wide transcription note over the Lumi Subdistrict languages, not an Eitiep-specific finding.
